p1s.summary: The Discussion states the two named reagents' parent-duplex lengths a third time — 'For both reagents named here that transcript is wild-type *TFG*, at eight and nine base pairs' — and neither _every_site pattern in test_journal_article_numbers.py reaches it. Swapping eight and nine there leaves the Abstract, section 2 and Table 1 green, which is precisely the harm that file's own docstring says it exists to prevent ('A reader ordering from the prose would get the wrong molecule for the patient in front of them').
p1s.evidence: Re-run at the pin against the flattened prose: pattern r"The \*?EWSR1\*? reagent's longest wild-type parent duplex through the whole gap is\s*(\w+) base pairs and the \*?TAF15\*? reagent's is (\w+)" returns exactly one match (section 2, line 144-146); pattern r"longest wild-type parent[\w\s-]{0,20}duplexes[\w\s]{0,20}?(\w+) and (\w+) base pairs" returns exactly one match (the Abstract, line 48-49). The Discussion sentence at lines 333-334 matches neither — it carries no 'longest wild-type parent ... duplexes' stem within the pattern's 20-character windows. Values are correct at the pin: fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv rows 167 and 565 give mature_parent_duplex_through_gap_bp 8 and 9, gene TFG.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Swapping 'eight and nine' to 'nine and eight' in the Discussion sentence alone, or copy-editing that sentence to attribute the eight to the TAF15 reagent. Every gate stays green and the Discussion then contradicts Table 1 and section 2.
p1s.artifact: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md (Discussion, 'The falsification experiment'), propagated into all four PDF builds

p1s.summary: The article names *TFG* as the gene supplying both named reagents' longest wild-type parent duplex at two prose sites (section 2 'both against wild-type *TFG*'; Discussion 'that transcript is wild-type *TFG*'). No test compares that gene name to the artifact that decides it. _TABLE1_ROW captures the duplex digits and swallows the gene inside a [^|]* run, so the table guard cannot see it either.
p1s.evidence: test_journal_article_numbers.py: _TABLE1_ROW = ... r"\|\s*(?P<duplex>\d+)\s*bp[^|]*\|" — the gene is inside [^|]* and is never a named group; the two _every_site patterns for this claim capture only (\w+) numerals. A repository-wide grep for 'TFG' across research/manuscripts/tests/ and research/modalities/tests/ returns no assertion that reads the ARTICLE's gene name; test_aso_sequence_manifest_joins.py:151 asserts lead['mature_parent_duplex_gene'] == 'TFG' but reads fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv, not the manuscript. The correct value at the pin is TFG for both (CSV rows 167, 565).
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Changing '*TFG*' to any other parent gene at either prose site. The Discussion's whole point in that sentence — that the pre-registered threshold is blind to a gene neither fusion involves — turns on the gene being a non-parent of the fusion, so a swap to *EWSR1* or *NR4A3* would silently invert the argument with nothing red.

p2s.summary: 'It is specified here for these reagents, with the two screened controls above; a knockdown assay alone separates none of the failure modes they exist to separate.' The antecedent of 'they' is unrecoverable. Read as the controls' own capability, the sentence is false (a scramble control in a knockdown assay is exactly what separates sequence-independent from sequence-specific effects) and it contradicts the next paragraph, which specifies a knockdown assay as the falsification test and computes its power. Read as 'a knockdown assay unaccompanied by these controls', it is true and is an argument FOR the controls. A referee cannot tell which the paper means, at the paper's central deliverable. What a true sentence would have to assert: which failure modes the two screened scrambles are there to separate, and that a knockdown readout WITHOUT them cannot separate those — not that the specified assay cannot.
p2s.evidence: git log -L 314,318 on the manuscript: the sentence read 'with three controls a knockdown assay alone cannot distinguish, two of them the screened scrambles above' before 5df4c45bc, became '...which a knockdown assay alone cannot distinguish' (5df4c45bc), then '...separates none of the failure modes those controls exist to separate' (ba0ab8b1f), and finally lost its explicit antecedent when a294fee68 replaced 'those controls' with 'they' as a word-count edit. The following paragraph (lines 319-334) defines selectivity as a ratio of two half-maximal knockdown concentrations from a matched dose-response and gives its power at 3, 6 and 10 replicates.

p2s.summary: The title advertises 'a pre-registrable knockdown experiment'. The specified decision rule is defined on the acceptor parent alone, and the paper states in the same paragraph that for BOTH named reagents the largest predicted parent liability is wild-type TFG, at 8 and 9 bp. The text says TFG is 'one to read alongside the acceptor' but gives no threshold, no readout and no decision rule for it, so the pre-registration as written cannot fail on the liability the paper's own screens flag hardest. This is disclosed rather than hidden, so it is a suggestion — but it is the first thing a referee will ask to see specified.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript lines 331-334. Confirmed against fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv rows 167 and 565 (mature_parent_duplex_gene = TFG, 8 bp and 9 bp) and research/modalities/aso-parent-gap-pairing.json corpus.which_parent_supplies_it, in which TFG supplies 6 of the 87 panel liabilities.

p2s.summary: In the committed .md — which is itself deposited in the archive at doi:10.5281/zenodo.22182180 — '## References' (line 417) is immediately followed by '## Tables' with nothing between, while the body carries 24 superscript citations. The Tables section names its sibling file ('Tables 1 and 2 are in `fusion-junction-aso-journal-tables.md`'); the References section names nothing, and the front matter's `related:` lists only DOC-FUSION-JUNCTION-ASO-SUBMISSION. A reader who opens the deposited markdown cannot resolve a single citation from it or discover where the list lives. Not a blocker: all four PDF builds carry the full 24-entry list.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript lines 417-422. fusion-junction-aso-journal-references.md exists at the pin with entries 1-24 and is in the archive manifest's file list. pdfminer extraction of fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.pdf, -manuscript.pdf, -preprint.pdf and -anonymized.pdf shows entries 1 through 24 present in all four.

p2s.summary: 'Ten is a convention, not a measurement: exon-terminus chimeras meet the same screen at 40.6% against the panel's 45.8%.' The colon asserts the chimera comparison is the ground for calling ten a convention. It is not: the chimera result says the panel's liability rate is not distinguishable from a null built from two real exon termini, which is a separate and independently important concession. Both facts are correct; the causal join between them is not.
p2s.evidence: research/modalities/aso-parent-null.json: null_ensembles.exon_terminus_chimera.rate_liable = 0.40568, observed.rate_liable = 0.45789, observed.rate_liable_wilson95 = [0.38859, 0.52887]. The artifact's own cut_sensitivity field grounds 'ten is adopted' separately, in method.min_duplex_bp and in the manuscript's Methods ('ten being adopted rather than measured').

p2s.summary: 'The two reagents named for synthesis are the best available designs at the two junctions with a published exon-resolved breakpoint and the highest reported prevalence.' The article never states the rule that makes one of five registers 'best available at this junction', so a reader cannot reproduce the selection from the text. The canonical record warns explicitly that the obvious guess is wrong.
p2s.evidence: fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv header: '`role` IS THE SELECTION COLUMN. ... Ranking on gap_level_margin is NOT the paper's rule: this file keys a row to 43 distinct junctions, 42 of them carry a 5-6-5 register, and over those 42 the rule returns a do_not_order design at 8 — at 5 of which a clean register was available and the rule did not pick it.' Both named reagents do sit at the panel's maximum gap_level_margin of 3 (computed over the 176 panel rows: margins are 1, 2 or 3, max 3), which is what makes margin the guess a reader will make.

p2s.summary: The Abstract says the work is 'executing an industry off-target framework's in-silico step'. The Introduction says the framework sets five steps, 'only the first is even partly in silico', and 'This work performs the in-silico half of the first step and stops there'. The abstract's compression reads as completing a whole step of the framework; the body says it is half of one of five.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript lines 45 (abstract) and 93-96 (Introduction), both citing reference 14 / PMID 39912803.

p2s.summary: The article states only 'phosphorothioate throughout, with wings of five contiguous β-D-oxy-locked residues' and directs ordering to fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv. The specification a synthesis vendor actually needs — 5-methylcytosine on locked cytosines against unmethylated 2'-deoxycytidine in the gap, free 5'/3' hydroxyl termini, no cap, sodium salt, stereorandom backbone — exists only in that file's header prose. The instruction is honest and the file does carry it, so nothing is wrong; but the CSV header attributes the specification to 'SECTION 6 OF THE MANUSCRIPT', a section this article does not have.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript lines 166-174 and 388-391; fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv header block 'CHEMISTRY — THE FULL SPECIFICATION, FROM SECTION 6 OF THE MANUSCRIPT.' The journal article's headings are Abstract, Keywords, Introduction, Materials and Methods, Results, Discussion, Acknowledgments, Author Disclosure Statement, Statements and Declarations, References, Tables, Figure legends — none numbered.

leakage: TWO disclosures. (1) The harness injected CLAUDE.md into my context as project instructions before I read the brief; CLAUDE.md is on the MAY-NOT-READ list. What it carried that touches this paper is its section 6 record of the 2026-08-27 mutation incident, which quotes four inverted sentences from this manuscript including 'Three designs clear every screen, each at a junction patients are reported to carry'. I scoped every later search away from it and re-derived that claim end to end from fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv (the 9 panel designs with mature_parent_duplex_through_gap_bp = 0 and the one at 8 bp against NR4A3, GGGCATATCAAGCGCT at TCF12_e7__NR4A3_e3; none of their junctions carries clinical_tier published_exon_resolved_breakpoint) and from the five published-tier junctions computed independently as EWSR1 e12, EWSR1 e13, TAF15 e6, TCF12 e5, TFG e7. I raise no finding on it. (2) A repository-wide grep returned four lines from research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-guard-coverage-audit.md, which is plausibly an earlier review seat's output though it is not named *-redteam*. The lines showed a mutation record for the same 'three designs' sentence and a note that the '47 of 183' derivation is bound to the extended report only. I had already derived 47 of 183 independently by re-running the censoring computation over the 38 orientation-filtered screens indexed in junction-aso-offtarget-locus-collapse.json (190 rows, 7 with no returned count, 47 of the remaining 183 with a hit list of 15 or fewer), and I raise no finding from that file. ONE THING I COULD NOT VERIFY: zenodo.org and doi.org are both blocked by this sandbox's egress proxy (curl exit 56, WebFetch EGRESS_BLOCKED), so I did not independently confirm that 10.5281/zenodo.22182180 resolves to a published record. I relied on the brief's stated state fact and on deposit-state.json's read-back block; the archive manifest's 515-file inventory, its empty promises_resolving_to_no_file list, and the presence of the article, tables, references and sequences.csv in that inventory I did check at the pin.
